## Module Overview

### Module summary

<!-- TODO(JWT): cite the steady-state utilization distribution method (named in the module's description) once it is in citations/. -->

caribou_SSUD maps caribou habitat use from an integrated step-selection analysis (iSSA).
It turns the model's fixed-effect coefficients into a steady-state utilization distribution: the long-run density of use the model's habitat and movement terms imply over a landscape.
The result is a probability density of use (PDE) for each model, normalized to sum to 1 over the area it is predicted for, and a binned map of it (`pdeMap`) that compares the cells within that area.

It handles two caribou ecotypes (`ecotype`): northern mountain caribou, whose coefficients are read from the fixed-effect table of a fitted model, and boreal caribou, whose `glmmTMB` models are supplied one per jurisdiction.
With `simulationScale` it maps the global model, one model per region, or both.

In static mode (`simulationProcess = "static"`, the default) it maps the baseline landscape only.
In dynamic mode it also rebuilds the landscape layers that change during a simulation -- the forest, from the simulated tree cohorts, and the time since fire -- every `predictionInterval` years from `predictStartYear`, and maps habitat use on each.

### Module inputs and parameters

The module needs the model and the landscape the model reads (Table \@ref(tab:moduleInputs-caribou-SSUD)):

- `iSSAcoefficients`, the northern mountain model's fixed-effect coefficients; if not supplied, they are read from `<coefficientsModel>_fixed.csv` in the model's zip file in the Google Drive folder `modelsFolderID`.
  Boreal models are supplied as `iSSAmodels`.
- `modelLand`, the landscape layers, named as in the model's terms; a layer the model needs and the list lacks stops the run, naming it.
- `studyAreaCaribou`, the area the global model was fit on, and, for the regional models, `studyArea_juris`, one area per region.
- Optionally, a baseline made earlier (`pde` and `pdeMap`, or a folder, zip file or URL in `baselineSource`), so the baseline is read rather than made again.

In dynamic mode it also needs the simulated forest (`cohortData` and `pixelGroupMap`), the time since fire (`timeSinceFire`) and the simulation's grid (`rasterToMatch`), which every `modelLand` layer must match.

```{r moduleInputs-caribou-SSUD, echo = FALSE, eval = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
df_inputs <- SpaDES.core::moduleInputs("caribou_SSUD", "..")
knitr::kable(df_inputs,
             caption = "List of (ref:caribou-SSUD) input objects and their description.")
```

The parameters (Table \@ref(tab:moduleParams-caribou-SSUD)) choose the ecotype, the models and the area each is mapped over (`ecotype`, `simulationScale`, `pdeArea`), static or dynamic mode and the prediction years (`simulationProcess`, `predictStartYear`, `predictionInterval`, `predictLastYear`), and where the model and a premade baseline come from (`coefficientsModel`, `modelsFolderID`, `baselineSource`).
`ts_else` is the time since disturbance given to cells with no recorded fire; use the value the model was fit with.


```{r moduleParams-caribou-SSUD, echo = FALSE, eval = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
df_params <- SpaDES.core::moduleParams("caribou_SSUD", "..")
knitr::kable(df_params, caption = "List of (ref:caribou-SSUD) parameters and their description.")
```

### Events

- `init`: makes the baseline PDE and map for the current landscape, or reads a premade one, and saves a baseline it made to the output folder.
  In dynamic mode it also schedules the two events below, from `predictStartYear` every `predictionInterval` years, and in the last year when `predictLastYear` is `TRUE`.
- `simLayers` (dynamic mode): rebuilds the layers that change -- the proportion of forest, from the simulated cohorts classified into forest types, and the time since fire, where cells that never burned get `ts_else` -- on top of the layers that do not (`fixedSSUD`), and writes the stack.
- `calcSimPde` (dynamic mode): maps habitat use on the rebuilt layers with the same models as the baseline, into `simPde` and `simPdeMap`, and writes them.

### Plotting

The module does not plot.

### Saving

A baseline the module makes is written to `pde_<.studyAreaName>/` in the output folder, as `pde_<model>.tif` and, when `normalizePDE` is `TRUE`, `pdeMap_<model>.tif`; each file is registered as an output.
In dynamic mode, each prediction year's layers and maps go to its `sims/` subfolder.

### Module outputs

Description of the module outputs (Table \@ref(tab:moduleOutputs-caribou-SSUD)).

```{r moduleOutputs-caribou-SSUD, echo = FALSE, eval = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
df_outputs <- SpaDES.core::moduleOutputs("caribou_SSUD", "..")
knitr::kable(df_outputs, caption = "List of (ref:caribou-SSUD) outputs and their description.")
```

### Links to other modules

In dynamic mode, the simulated forest comes from the LandR Biomass modules (`Biomass_core`: `cohortData` and `pixelGroupMap`) and the time since fire from the fire model (e.g. `scfm`).
The coefficients and the landscape layers come from the iSSA fit, made outside SpaDES (e.g. with `hsaCEtool`).
